patterns_data.pattern_details: Spend growth is highly concentrated in a small set of providers rather than evenly spread across the network. Yale New Haven Hospital is the dominant driver in CT PPO acute hospital business, while Lakeview, Greenleaf, and Elkhart show smaller but recurring admission concentration in GA behavioral health and IN acute hospital business. This points to provider-specific contracting, steerage, and utilization management opportunities rather than a broad marketwide trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When a few providers account for a disproportionate share of growth, provider-level action can move results faster than broad policy changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run provider-specific action plans for Yale New Haven Hospital, Lakeview Behavioral Health, Greenleaf Behavioral Health Hospital, and Elkhart General Hospital that combine contract review, admission pattern review, and steerage or case-management controls.
evidence_summary: Yale New Haven Hospital in CT PPO acute hospital business drove +$16.7M, with 176 more admissions and about +$18.3K paid per admit.
Lakeview and Greenleaf in GA added about +$0.4M from 162 more admissions combined, even as paid per admit fell.
Elkhart General Hospital in IN added about +$0.4M across HMO and POS acute hospital volume growth, with 38 more admissions combined.
GA IP BH psychoses cases added about +$0.3M across Lakeview and Greenleaf, reinforcing provider concentration.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Beyond the top named providers, inpatient hospital spend is rising across KY and the CA / CO / GA / NH / NV / NY / TX segment, with smaller additions from CA / IN / VA, TX / WI, and CA / MO. KY shows both HMO volume growth and PPO unit-cost pressure, while several other markets show the same mix of more admissions and higher paid per case. This is a recurring inpatient pressure pattern that needs coordinated utilization and reimbursement action by market.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is a broad inpatient cost trend, so leaving it unaddressed risks sustained spend growth across multiple products and markets.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Build a market-by-market inpatient action plan starting with KY and the CA / CO / GA / NH / NV / NY / TX segment, pairing admission management with rate and payment review for craniotomy, neuro, delivery, and chemotherapy-related cases.
evidence_summary: KY HMO acute hospital business added +$5.8M with 196 more admissions; KY PPO acute hospital business added +$2.1M even with 38 fewer admissions because paid per admit rose about $15.9K.
The CA / CO / GA / NH / NV / NY / TX HMO acute hospital segment added +$6.2M, led by craniotomy cases in GA (+$1.4M) and CO (+$1.3M).
CA EPO acute hospital business added +$2.1M in craniotomy cases with 14 more admissions.
CA / IN / VA HMO, TX / WI POS, CA / MO PPO, and KY CHILDRENS added about +$6.2M more, largely from volume-led craniotomy, delivery, chemotherapy, and neuro activity.

patterns_data.pattern_details: ME HMO acute hospital spend increased because admissions rose sharply, not because hospital prices increased. The utilization signal is strong enough to warrant immediate admission management attention, but ME also has a separate auth-classification issue that should be cleared before treating the full change as purely clinical demand. This is primarily an access, admission, and authorization workflow issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A large volume-led spike can quickly reset the inpatient cost base if utilization controls are not tightened.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: First validate the ME auth classification shift, then run an admission-level utilization review on the ME HMO acute hospital surge to identify avoidable admissions and tighten front-end authorization controls.
patterns_data.validation_reason: ME also has a separate auth-code-distribution validation finding, so classification should be confirmed before attributing the full increase to true utilization.
evidence_summary: ME HMO acute hospital business added +$14.7M on 410 more admissions.
Average paid per admit fell about $36.6K, so the increase was volume-led rather than price-led.
Claim count rose by 213, reinforcing that the pattern is broad utilization growth rather than isolated high-cost cases.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Several findings point to spend moving between auth buckets or into unmapped facility categories rather than reflecting a clean business trend. The issue is concentrated in ME, CA, GA / TX / WI, and in unmapped facility classifications in KY, IN / TX, and CT. This should be treated as a gating data and workflow validation issue before changing policy, contracts, or UM rules.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If auth or facility fields are shifting, the organization can misread where cost is truly rising and take action in the wrong place.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit PA indicator logic and facility mapping across claims and authorization feeds for ME, CA, GA / TX / WI, KY, IN / TX, and CT, and hold downstream policy or contracting changes until the fields reconcile.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The source groups explicitly flag auth or mapping shifts and require validation before action.
evidence_summary: ME auth-code distribution showed -$3.4M of apparent movement without a matching utilization or unit-cost read.
CA auth-code distribution added +$1.3M, and GA / TX / WI added another +$1.3M in apparent auth-bucket shifts.
Unmapped facility growth added +$1.2M in KY HMO, plus smaller impacts in IN / TX and CT.
These findings carry explicit validation flags and should be cleared before contracting or UM action.

key_driver_codes: Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System with MCC
Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with Spinal Curvature, Malignancy, Infection or Extensive Fusions with CC
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC

patterns_data.pattern_details: A small number of extremely expensive Med/Surg cases generated a disproportionate share of spend growth. These include transplant, complex neuro, spine infection and fusion, and cardiac surgery runs that often occurred on only 2 to 4 admissions but carried very high paid amounts per admit. This is not a broad utilization trend; it is a concentrated catastrophic-case pattern that needs case-level review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can distort total cost trends and may expose gaps in outlier payment handling, clinical review, or case management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform case-level medical and payment review on these transplant, complex neuro, spine, and cardiac outlier claims to confirm severity, benefit coverage, and outlier reimbursement handling.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The source groups are repeatedly flagged as low baseline or small-n, so case-level confirmation is needed before broad action.
evidence_summary: A spinal infection and complex fusion run added +$2.1M on 2 admissions, or about $1.1M paid per admit.
Yale heart transplant or heart-assist cases added +$1.4M on 2 admissions, or about $0.7M paid per admit.
CA rare craniotomy and neurosurgical cases added +$4.1M, including subdural hematoma (+$1.0M) and cranial nerve tumor cases (+$0.8M).
These groups are all flagged as low baseline or small-n, so case-level review is needed before broad policy moves.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Physical Rehab, LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL, CRITICAL ACCESS, and NF settings
key_driver_codes: Physical Rehab
LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL
CRITICAL ACCESS
NF
Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC

patterns_data.pattern_details: Recovery and aftercare cases are showing up more often in post-acute and alternative inpatient settings, especially rehab, LTCH, critical access, and NF. The pattern is strongest in TX and CA, with added pressure in CT, IN, NH, and NY. This suggests a site-of-care and discharge-routing issue rather than only acute hospital unit-cost inflation.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When recovery episodes move into higher-cost post-acute settings, total episode cost can rise quickly even if acute hospital stays are stable.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review post-acute placement rules, discharge planning, and reimbursement terms for rehab, LTCH, NF, and critical access cases, starting with TX and CA, to determine whether lower-cost recovery pathways can be used more consistently.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several contributing groups are small-volume or low-baseline runs, so confirm true site-of-care movement before broad network changes.
evidence_summary: CA EPO LTCH added +$0.6M on 2 more admissions, with about +$288.5K paid per admit.
TX HMO Physical Rehab added +$0.4M from 20 more admissions, while TX HMO and POS rehab aftercare added another +$0.4M.
NH / NY HMO rehab and CA / CT PPO LTCH added about +$0.7M combined in small but high-cost runs.
TX clinical aftercare and hemiplegia cases added about +$4.2M across recovery-oriented pathways.

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX delivery episodes are showing higher complexity, with gestational diabetes, prior C-section scar-related care, fetal distress, and gestational hypertension contributing to higher spend. CT also shows added delivery volume on the PPO acute hospital side. The business response here is focused maternity pathway management rather than general inpatient cost control.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity episodes are common enough that even modest increases in complexity and delivery volume can materially raise inpatient spend.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Target OB case management and medical policy review in TX and CT for gestational diabetes, prior C-section scar-related maternity care, fetal distress, and gestational hypertension episodes, and test whether earlier intervention can reduce inpatient complexity.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several TX maternity drivers are flagged as low-baseline or small-n, so confirm emerging case mix before broad policy changes.
evidence_summary: TX delivery complication cases added about +$0.9M, led by gestational diabetes in childbirth (+$0.3M) and other third-trimester complications (+$0.3M).
TX OB volume and intensity added another +$0.2M from fetal distress and gestational hypertension cases.
Prior C-section scar-related maternity care added about +$0.1M in TX.
CT PPO vaginal delivery volume added +$0.3M on 28 more admissions.

patterns_data.top_pattern: WI inpatient chemotherapy is becoming a distinct cost driver
key_driver_codes: Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
ENCOUNTER FOR ANTINEOPLASTIC CHEMO
patterns_data.pattern_details: WI shows a distinct inpatient chemotherapy pattern rather than a broad Med/Surg trend. The increase reflects both more admissions and higher paid per admit, making this an oncology-specific utilization and care-setting question. The likely business lever is inpatient oncology appropriateness and episode management, not general acute hospital policy.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Oncology episodes often need separate medical policy and case-management rules because their admission drivers differ from general Med/Surg.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review WI inpatient chemotherapy admissions for medical necessity, site-of-care appropriateness, and episode management opportunities specific to oncology.
evidence_summary: WI inpatient chemotherapy added +$1.1M on 42 more admissions.
Paid per admit rose by about $6.4K, so the change was not volume alone.
The increase is concentrated in a single chemotherapy episode type rather than spread across many diagnoses.
